newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burmese stage anti-Rangoon protest at Thai camp.
newsitem.headline: Burmese stage anti-Rangoon protest at Thai camp.

text.p: About 150 Burmese students and refugees on Tuesday staged a demonstration inside a detention centre in central Thailand to denounce the suppression of student street protests in Rangoon early this month.

The protestors, carrying banners and shouting slogans against the ruling Burmese State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), said they would stage a 24-hour protest at the camp, which houses about 870 refugees.
"We condemn ferocious arrests and suppression by the military junta on the peaceful gathering of students and people on December 2-3," said a statement by the protestors.
"There is a great tradition of students, those who sacrificed their lives courageously for want of peace and freedom in defiance to unjust ruling bodies," it added.
Nearly 2,000 Burmese university students took to the streets in Rangoon early this month in the biggest anti-government protest seen in the Burmese capital since the prodemocracy uprisings of 1988.

Burmese authorities broke up the protests, triggered by student demands for greater freedom. They were also protesting against alleged police brutality during a brawl in October between some students and restaurant owners.
More than 860 students were briefly detained for questioning after the protests, which prompted the SLORC to indefinitely suspend classes at all institutes of higher learning in Rangoon.

In a separate statement, exiled Burmese students of the All Burma's Students for Democratic Front (ABSDF), said on Tuesday that the SLORC had forcibly relocated more than 25,000 villagers from 99 villages in southern Tenasserim Division since May.
But a Burmese government spokesman in Rangoon said the student charges were unfounded and denied there was any government move to relocate people in Tenasserim.
The exiled students oppose Burma's decision to let foreign oil companies, led by Total SA, build a natural gas pipeline through the Tenasserim area.

A spokesman for Thai-based ABSDF said the SLORC removed people from the three townships in the resource area because it was economically lucrative. The students alleged that 123 villagers died during the relocation in May and June.
He said most uprooted people were accused by the government of failing to comply with earlier SLORC orders for them to report on activities of ethnic armed forces and exiled students.
The ABSDF spokesman urged foreign firms to not invest in Burma.
